title: Put both AirPods Pro back in their case, each stem-first into its own well, and push the lid shut so its magnet holds it
instruction: Put both earbuds back in their charging case and close the lid.
context: Most people with wireless earbuds put them back in their case several times a day, and the case charges them, and shuts, only when each bud sits fully in its own well. The two wells are mirror images, so each bud goes only into its own side's well, stem first and the right way round: its stem has to go down the well's narrow bore, and only over the last few millimetres does the well's magnet pull it home. A bud in the wrong well, or let go before its stem is down the bore, sits proud, and the lid then rests open on it instead of snapping shut. The case is light and narrow, and a push on its open lid tips it, so the other hand holds it while the lid is pushed over and shut. Here an AirPods Pro 2 case stands open on the table and both buds lie beside it. Apple, AirPods and AirPods Pro are trademarks of Apple Inc., named for identification only.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. An Apple AirPods Pro 2 MagSafe Charging Case (Apple: 45.2 x 60.6 x 21.7 mm, 50.8 g) stands upright on the bench centred at (34, 2), its 60.6 mm width along y, its lid hinged along its far (+x) top edge and open at 115 degrees (Apple's drawing), leaning back away from the robot. Its top holds two wells, centred 17 mm either side of the case's centre, the left bud's at +y and the right bud's at -y, so the seated heads stand about 12 mm apart. Each well is a bore shaped to the bud's stem (5.7 x 7.6 mm, 23.3 mm long) with 0.75 to 0.8 mm of play a side and a chamfered mouth (2.5 mm a side, 4 mm deep), plus two key slots over its top: one for the rib on the stem's outer side (standing 2.2 mm off the stem) and one for the bump on its front. So each bud goes only into its own well, stem first, front toward the robot; in the other well its rib meets solid wall with the bud still 6 mm or more proud. A seated bud's head rests on the rim, 7.6 mm proud of it, and the shut lid clears it by 1.4 mm. Each well's magnet pulls a bud whose seat is within 7 mm of home toward the seat with 0.4 N, and not from farther away; the lid's magnet pulls it shut over its last 5 degrees and holds it with 1 N at its edge. The two AirPods Pro 2 earbuds (Apple: 30.9 x 21.8 x 24.0 mm, 5.3 g each; bud head 17.3 mm deep: Apple's 24.0 mm includes the silicone ear tip, which squashes in the real case and is not modelled) lie on their sides on the bench, stem toward the robot (-x), front up: the left one at (26, 14) and the right one at (26, 22). Frictions: case on bench 0.4, buds 0.5. Well, bore, key, magnet, hinge and friction figures are estimates from maker photos (Apple publishes none). The case may be held or lifted, as long as it never tips past 20 degrees; where it ends counts. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset: buds back on their marks, front up; lid open at 115 degrees.
scoring: Judged once both grippers are at least 3 cm from the case and everything has been still for 1 s. A bud is seated when it is in its own well within 0.5 mm of fully home, 1 mm of its axis in each direction, 5 degrees of upright and 10 degrees of its turn (real trial: turn the open case upside down and both buds stay in). The lid is shut when it is closed within 1 degree (real trial: turn the closed case upside down and the lid stays shut). Each bud seated in its own well: 0.25. Lid shut over both seated buds: 0.5 more. The case must end upright within 5 degrees and within 3 cm of where it stood; if it ends elsewhere, is ever tipped past 20 degrees, or a bud leaves the bench: 0. The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (150 s at 20 Hz), about 2.6 times the 58 s demo
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the case at its mark with the lid open at 115 degrees, both buds on their marks lying on their sides, front up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Case and buds at Apple's published sizes and masses; bud head 17.3 mm deep: Apple's 24.0 mm includes the silicone ear tip, which squashes in the real case and is not modelled. Wells, keys, hinge and frictions are estimates. Each well's magnet is code: a 0.4 N pull toward its seat, only within 7 mm of it, the case taking the reaction. The lid's magnet is a drive in its own hinge: 1 N at its edge over the last 5 degrees. The demo reads object poses and the lid's angle.
scores: Dream-1: 0 (3,000 steps, one session); demo: 1.0 (both hands, 1,163 steps); one hand alone: 0.0 (the lid push tips the unheld case over); buds swapped: 0.0; one bud left on the bench: 0.25.
